title: Efficient Learning of Fermionic Magic States under Free-Fermion Evolution
authors: Jiwon Heo, Myeongjin Shin, Changhun Oh
abstract: We establish efficient learning for a family of fermionic magic states under unknown number-conserving free-fermion evolution. Each input block has a definite particle number and is a superposition of Fock states, with occupied mode sets disjoint both within and across blocks. The key idea is to exploit the spectral structure of particle reduced density matrices (RDMs) to separate contributions from individual blocks from those involving several blocks, allowing us to reconstruct the hidden block structure. For a fixed upper bound on the particle number per block, our algorithm uses single-copy measurements and polynomial sample and classical computational complexity to recover a compact description of the state with prescribed fidelity and high probability, without prior knowledge of the block decomposition or the evolution. RDMs up to this upper bound suffice for reconstruction. We further show that this RDM order is necessary in general: two orthogonal states in the family can have identical RDMs at every lower order. These results show that an extensive number of non-Gaussian blocks can be compatible with efficient state learning.
summary: This paper develops an efficient quantum information protocol to reconstruct a fermionic magic state $|\Psiangle$ that results from an unknown free-fermion evolution $\hat{U}$ acting on a structured input state $|\Psi_{	ext{in}}angle$. It achieves this by leveraging the spectral properties of particle reduced density matrices (RDMs) to decompose the state into its constituent blocks. The result demonstrates that the state can be learned with polynomial complexity, providing a powerful tool for characterizing complex quantum many-body states.
main_problem: The paper establishes efficient methods to learn a compact description of a fermionic magic state $|\Psiangle$ that results from applying an unknown free-fermion evolution ($\hat{U}$) to a structured input state $|\Psi_{	ext{in}}angle$.
main_result: The authors show that this learning can be achieved using single-copy measurements and polynomial complexity by exploiting the spectral structure of particle reduced density matrices (RDMs).
method: The core method involves recursively analyzing and reconstructing the state by utilizing the $k$-RDM ($\Gamma^{(k)}$) to separate contributions from different input blocks, followed by classical post-processing like Gram-splitting.
model_or_system: The system is a fermionic model described by creation and annihilation operators ($\hat{c}^\dagger, \hat{c}$) acting on $m$ modes. The state $|\Psiangle$ is generated by a passive Gaussian unitary $\hat{U}$ acting on a structured input state $|\Psi_{	ext{in}}angle$ composed of disjoint fermionic blocks.
key_observables: Particle reduced density matrices ($\Gamma^{(k)}_\Psi$), fidelity ($\epsilon_{	ext{fid}}$), and the reconstructed state $	ilde{\Psi}$.
important_parameters: The required RDM order ($r$) is bounded by the maximum particle number per block; complexity depends polynomially on $m$ and $1/\epsilon_{	ext{fid}}$.
main_assumptions: The input blocks have a definite, bounded particle number, and the analysis relies on the spectral properties of the RDMs to decompose the state structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the input state family ($\vert\Psi_{	ext{in}}angle$) and the target state ($\vert\Psiangle$), showing how local mode sets define blocks and how the target state is obtained via the unitary $\hat{U}$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem (learning $\hat{U}|\Psi_{	ext{in}}angle$) to developing the mathematical tools (exploiting RDM spectral structure), proving the existence of efficient algorithms for both homogeneous and heterogeneous block structures, and finally bounding the preparation error and complexity.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for characterizing and simulating complex quantum states generated by free-fermion dynamics, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum simulation algorithms and resource estimation in quantum information.
